decisions.executionNote: Charger and strip are both on the left. Begin left-arm elevated approach, keeping right at origin; plan a grasp from the charger's upper end for upright insertion.
Advance the left wrist above the objects while turning the open gripper toward the charger's USB end; keep elevated clearance.
Reduce increments after continuity rejection; continue elevated left approach with gradual wrist turn.
Continue above the left objects, increasing downward approach angle for clearance over the nearby strip.
Keep the open left gripper elevated while moving around to the far end of the charger, gradually pitching down and turning.
Smaller wrist increments after guard rejection; move toward the far side of the charger with the gripper open and clear of the strip.
Turn toward the charger from its far end while maintaining height and elbow-up continuity; fine alignment will use the wrist view.
Reduce yaw rate after continuity rejection and increase downward tilt to move away from the wrist's difficult configuration.
Continue a slow elevated turn and far-side approach; inspect the open gripper and charger alignment before descent.
Rotate the open left gripper gradually toward the charger's long axis while moving to a clear far-side pregrasp.
Continue far-side pregrasp alignment with small joint-continuous increments, remaining above the strip.
Complete more of the far-end yaw alignment while lowering only slightly, leaving clearance until charger appears centered in the wrist view.
Slowly finish orienting toward the charger from its upper end; maintain clearance while bringing it into the wrist camera.
Align the gripper with the charger's long axis from the USB end, descending conservatively toward the body.
Hold yaw after the wrist-limit rejection. Center the charger between the open fingers using a small leftward and downward approach.
Charger is now centered in the wrist view. Approach its sides in millimeter increments, slightly unwinding yaw to preserve wrist-limit margin.
Close the left gripper around the aligned charger body and begin a small test lift; retention must be confirmed visually.
Maintain full closure and allow the grasp to settle, then lift a few millimeters to check whether the charger follows.
The charger appears captured between the fingers. Lift clear of the tabletop while maintaining closure before reorienting the pins downward.
Retention is visible after lift. Begin rotating the charger pins downward while compensating wrist translation to keep the body clear of the table.
Raise the retained charger farther from the table and continue controlled pin-down rotation toward the strip, keeping the right arm parked.
Continue pin-down rotation with the charger visibly retained, shifting slightly left and toward the strip while preserving table clearance.
Keep the charger securely closed and continue rotating its pins toward vertical; compensate the wrist path to position it above the middle socket.
Finish approaching upright orientation in smaller increments, holding the charger above the strip rather than inserting while tilted.
Bring the charger close to vertical while holding insertion height. Use the exposed socket pattern to refine alignment next.
Correct a small residual charger tilt and translate left over the socket, descending only partway to regain a clear alignment view.
Refine lateral alignment toward the exposed socket and lower conservatively, with a small yaw correction to match the two-prong row.
The wrist is at its rotation limit. Lift away and start a continuous half-turn about the upright charger, preserving retention and avoiding a joint-branch switch.
Continue the upright half-turn with wrist-limit margin; arc the wrist around the retained charger rather than sweeping the charger across the table.
Continue the clearance-height yaw arc around the retained upright charger; do not descend until the prong row matches the socket.
Maintain the upright charger at clearance height while continuing the joint-continuous yaw arc toward socket alignment.
Continue the clearance-height turn, keeping the plug upright and held closed. The prong row still needs further yaw alignment.
Keep the charger upright at clearance height while completing more of the half-turn; maintain the closed grasp and left-workspace arc.
Finish the larger yaw correction at clearance height. The upright plug remains retained; next refine the socket alignment and descend.
Prong row now appears nearly parallel to the socket row. Approach the middle socket with small lateral correction and a partial descent, retaining the charger.
Refine the middle-socket alignment from the wrist and head views, correcting slightly right and nearer while descending in small steps.
Hold horizontal alignment and lower the upright charger toward the socket in small vertical increments, watching for contact or displacement.
Contact displaced the charger within the fingers, so back off before correcting. Lift slightly and refine lateral/prong-row alignment rather than pushing against the strip.
The exposed middle socket is still to the right of the two pins in the wrist view. Make a small lateral and yaw correction at the backed-off height.
Continue the small lateral correction toward the middle socket's outer two slots, with only a minimal descent while checking pin alignment.
The two pins now appear aligned with the middle socket's outer slots. Lower vertically by small increments while keeping the grasp closed.
Continue a gentle vertical insertion attempt with horizontal alignment fixed; watch for pin engagement and any charger motion within the fingers.
The charger shifted within the fingers during descent, suggesting contact before full engagement. Back off slightly and correct the pin row a few millimeters nearer before retrying.
The exposed slots allow finer alignment: shift the pin pair slightly left and toward the row, then lower a few millimeters with the grasp closed.
The pin pair is close to the middle socket row. Attempt a short vertical insertion while holding lateral position and monitoring for further slip.
The charger stayed fixed relative to the fingers during the last descent. Continue a short, straight insertion with no lateral sweep.
Make a very small backed-off centering correction to the visible prongs, then retry straight downward seating without forcing the strip.
Attempt the final few millimeters of straight seating with the two pins centered on the socket; monitor contact and retention before releasing.
Release the supported charger carefully after a tiny alignment correction, then lift clear to inspect whether it seats upright without gripper-induced tilt.
Withdraw the open gripper vertically to inspect the charger's unsupported orientation and insertion depth.
The released charger remains upright on the socket. Move the open left arm clear and begin a continuous elbow-up return toward origin, checking that the charger stays seated.
The charger has tipped after release, so it was not fully seated. Reposition the open left gripper above its USB end for a straighter regrasp and another insertion attempt.
Approach the fallen charger's USB end from the left workspace, adjusting the open gripper for a more axial grasp while staying clear of the strip.
Continue the open-gripper reorientation above the displaced charger, retaining left-workspace clearance and using a moderately downward axial approach.
Bring the left gripper toward the charger's exposed right end while finishing the axial approach orientation, remaining on the left side of the centerline.
Move the open left gripper toward the displaced charger from its right end, using the head view for approach because the wrist view is rolled.
Lower and offset the open gripper to align its grasp center with the charger's exposed end; the charger has entered the rolled wrist view.
Center the exposed USB end in the open fingers with small downward and lateral corrections, keeping the wrist on the left side.
Advance the aligned fingers a few millimeters around the USB-end sides, then close for a new axial grasp; verify retention before lifting.
Keep full closure for the axial grasp and perform a small vertical test lift to verify that the charger follows without the strip.
The axial grasp is retained in the wrist view. Lift clear and start bringing the charger axis vertical, moving the wrist left toward the strip.
Continue the retained axial-grasp rotation toward vertical while raising the charger and moving left over the strip.
Bring the axially held charger nearly vertical above the strip with continued clearance; retain full closure before matching the pin-row yaw.
Finish the axial vertical alignment and start matching the charger's width to the strip's socket row, staying above contact height.
Keep the charger vertical and lift slightly while matching its pin-row yaw to the visible socket row.
Continue the upright yaw correction at fixed clearance height; compare the charger face edge with the socket row before descent.
Fine-tune the upright charger's yaw and shift toward the socket row at clearance height; use the exposed sockets to refine centering before descent.
The charger face and socket row now appear parallel. Lower the axial grasp straight toward the middle socket, making only a tiny yaw refinement.
Refine centering above the middle socket by a few millimeters left and nearer, keeping the axial charger upright and at the current clearance height.
Make a small calibrated head-view correction toward the middle pin row and lower the vertical charger only a few millimeters, monitoring for contact.
Keep the axial charger upright and lower straight toward the socket by one centimeter, with no lateral sweep during possible engagement.
Continue straight axial seating in millimeter increments. The charger remains steady relative to the fingers; stop lateral motion during insertion.
Attempt the next five millimeters of vertical seating with fixed alignment, checking for slip or strip displacement before release.
Contact changed the charger orientation within the fingers. Back off a few millimeters and refine the pin-row yaw rather than forcing continued descent.
At the backed-off height, align the charger face edge with the socket row and shift a few millimeters toward that row before another short insertion.
The charger face is now parallel to the socket row. Attempt six millimeters of straight vertical seating with the grasp closed and no lateral sweep.
The charger stayed steady during the last descent. Continue a short, straight seating motion with the pin-row alignment fixed.
Allow a final millimeter of seating, then open and begin vertical withdrawal to check whether the charger remains upright and supported by the socket.
Withdraw the open gripper straight upward without touching the charger, and verify it remains upright before returning to origin.
Move the open arm clear of the strip along a continuous elbow-up return path while checking whether the released charger stays seated.
The charger has again tipped rather than remaining inserted. Reapproach above its far end for a controlled regrasp; do not assume the previous seating succeeded.
Align the open, downward-facing gripper over the charger's upper body, approaching from above with clearance from the socket strip.
Grasp the flat charger's upper body from above, keeping the fingers away from the prongs and strip; close fully before testing retention.
